preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.
Each of the n lines after the first contains exactly two elements: a coordinate and a type.

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'B', 'R', 'P'} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for c in [line.split()[1]])
preconditions.description: Each city type is either 'B' (Byteland), 'R' (Berland), or 'P' (disputed).

preconditions.expression: all(-10**9 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each city coordinate is between -10^9 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len({int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]}) == n
all(int(stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[0]) < int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()[0]) for i in range(n-1))
preconditions.description: Cities are given in strictly increasing order of their coordinates.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimal total cost of cables.

postconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[0]) in {int(stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[0]) for i in range(1, n+1) if stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[1] in {'B', 'P'}} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output corresponds to a set of cables that connects all Byteland and disputed cities (ignoring Berland cities).

postconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[0]) in {int(stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[0]) for i in range(1, n+1) if stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[1] in {'R', 'P'}} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output corresponds to a set of cables that connects all Berland and disputed cities (ignoring Byteland cities).

postconditions.expression: int(stdout) == min(total_cost for total_cost in possible_costs)
postconditions.description: The output is the minimal possible total cost of cables satisfying the connectivity conditions for both Byteland+disputed and Berland+disputed cities.
